findings.summary: The site ignores the user’s dark-color preference.
findings.evidence: The dark-mode screenshot is visually identical to the light page, and the computed root color-scheme remains “normal” under prefers-color-scheme: dark.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme and provide preference-driven dark surface, text, control, image, and browser-UI colors.

findings.summary: The hero video keeps autoplaying when reduced motion is requested.
findings.evidence: Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, the autoplay video remained unpaused and advanced from 3.145s to 4.646s in 1.5 seconds.
findings.suggestedFix: Replace autoplay motion with the poster under reduced motion, or pause it and offer an explicit play control.

findings.summary: Navigation does not expose a View Transitions treatment.
findings.evidence: DOM/CSS inspection found no ::view-transition styles, while representative navigation is conventional full-document replacement.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a progressively enhanced cross-document View Transition for stable shared chrome and route content, respecting reduced motion.

findings.summary: The fixed header does not communicate scroll state.
findings.evidence: Computed DOM evidence shows a fixed 72px nav, but CSS inspection found no scroll-state query or progress treatment across a 9,528px mobile page.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a scroll-state container query or a lightweight progress/shrinking treatment so long pages preserve context without consuming unnecessary space.

findings.summary: The cookie banner obscures the primary task on load.
findings.evidence: At 360×800 the banner occupies roughly the bottom third of the first viewport and covers the upload card; it also obscures pricing, API, blog, and signup content in retained screenshots.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a compact, non-obscuring consent surface with equal first-layer choices, preserve settings access, and avoid covering the primary action.

findings.summary: Largest Contentful Paint is far outside the good range.
findings.evidence: Mobile Lighthouse measured LCP 19.4s, FCP 2.8s, TBT 320ms and performance 0.56; the independent trace measured LCP 8.06s. The LCP video lacked fetchpriority=high.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritise the LCP poster/video discovery, reduce its bytes, add an appropriate fetch-priority hint, and defer non-critical work.

findings.summary: The mobile page shifts after initial rendering.
findings.evidence: The 360×800 layout observer recorded CLS 0.109 with a late shift at 5.54s; 26 of 27 images omit explicit width/height attributes.
findings.suggestedFix: Reserve image/media space with width/height or aspect-ratio and stabilise late consent/media insertion.

findings.summary: Main-thread work creates avoidable blocking.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured 320ms TBT; the trace found a 205ms long task and the layout observer recorded a 276ms long task.
findings.suggestedFix: Profile the long tasks, split work into smaller scheduled tasks, and defer code unrelated to the first interaction.

findings.summary: The landing page transfers a disproportionate 6.03MB.
findings.evidence: HAR evidence records 6,033,124 transferred bytes: 4.47MB images and 1.32MB scripts. A 1.96MB PNG and a 1.50MB PNG dominate transfer; the font stylesheet is parser-blocking.
findings.suggestedFix: Serve correctly sized AVIF/WebP responsive assets, avoid eager below-fold media, and shorten the critical font/resource chain.

findings.guidanceId: Large bundles contain mostly unused code.
findings.summary: Lighthouse estimates 791KiB unused JavaScript and 107KiB unused CSS; the main 943KB script is 65% unused and three stylesheets are 96–100% unused.
findings.evidence: Route-split application code and CSS, conditionally load editing and analytics dependencies, and remove duplicate/legacy payload.

findings.summary: Core controls and images have accessibility semantics defects.
findings.evidence: axe found critical missing labels on the before/after range input and missing alt text on two meaningful feature images; the image primitive found seven images without alt.
findings.suggestedFix: Give the range an accessible name and state, and add meaningful alt text or explicit presentation semantics as appropriate.

findings.summary: Cookie controls fail WCAG AA contrast.
findings.evidence: axe measured 3.78:1 for “Information & Settings” and “Reject all” against #c1e7c2, below the required 4.5:1.
findings.suggestedFix: Darken the consent text/control color or adjust its surface so normal text reaches at least 4.5:1.

findings.summary: A hidden language control remains focusable.
findings.evidence: axe and Lighthouse found a focusable “English” button inside aria-hidden=true, producing an accessibility-tree failure.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove hidden controls from the tab order, use inert/hidden for inactive UI, and restore focus only when the control becomes visible.

findings.summary: Image sizing and a deprecated media technique weaken platform hygiene.
findings.evidence: The images primitive found 26 images without dimensions and Lighthouse reported deprecated -internal-media-controls-overlay-cast-button usage.
findings.suggestedFix: Emit intrinsic image dimensions and replace the deprecated selector with disableRemotePlayback where needed.

findings.summary: Large first-party bundles lack usable source maps.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse could not obtain source maps for the large first-party JavaScript bundles, reducing production diagnosability.
findings.suggestedFix: Publish correct production source maps to an access-controlled error-monitoring path or make public maps available if policy permits.

findings.summary: The blog listing has no meta description.
findings.evidence: Rendered and raw profile evidence found a title and H1 for /blog but no meta[name=description].
findings.suggestedFix: Add a unique concise description for the blog index and verify all representative templates emit one server-side.

findings.summary: Rich pages omit structured entity metadata.
findings.evidence: The article, blog, pricing, and API profiles contain zero JSON-LD blocks. The article has descriptive visible content but no Article schema.
findings.suggestedFix: Add accurate JSON-LD for Article, Organization/WebSite, and applicable Product/Offer entities, matching visible content.

findings.summary: The main document has no Content-Security-Policy.
findings.evidence: Header evidence confirms HTTPS, HSTS, nosniff and X-Frame-Options, but Content-Security-Policy is absent.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy a nonce/hash-based CSP, start in Report-Only, then enforce least-privilege script/style/connect/frame policies.

findings.summary: The default page load has a broad third-party and analytics footprint.
findings.evidence: Tracker evidence found 9 third-party origins including Google Tag Manager and Google Analytics; HAR attributes 36 of 41 requests and 6.01MB to cross-origin hosts.
findings.suggestedFix: Reduce vendors, self-host stable assets where practical, defer analytics until allowed/needed, and batch minimised events.

findings.summary: Authentication offers passwords and federated login but no visible passkey path.
findings.evidence: The signup profile exposes password/new-password fields and Facebook/Google login; no WebAuthn/passkey control or credential-registration path was present. Permission prompts were not fired on load.
findings.suggestedFix: Offer passkey registration and sign-in alongside recovery-safe existing methods, with reauthentication for sensitive account actions.

findings.summary: Permissions Policy is absent and cookie scope is broader than necessary.
findings.evidence: Headers contain no Permissions-Policy; the first-party consent and session cookies use SameSite=None, although both are Secure and the session is HttpOnly.
findings.suggestedFix: Set a restrictive Permissions-Policy and use Lax/Strict SameSite where cross-site flows do not require None.

findings.summary: The no-JavaScript experience loses the core task and most content.
findings.evidence: Discoverability measured only 54% word coverage; the crawler screenshot contains only “Remove Image Background / 100% Automatically and” with no upload action, navigation, or supporting content.
findings.suggestedFix: Server-render the primary uploader shell, navigation and meaningful content, then enhance processing and editing with JavaScript.

findings.summary: The app advertises installability but has no offline worker or cache.
findings.evidence: A standalone web manifest is present, but after load navigator.serviceWorker.getRegistrations() returned none and Cache Storage was empty.
findings.suggestedFix: Register a service worker with a small offline shell/fallback and intentionally cache only safe static resources.

findings.summary: The multilingual UI is not built with writing-mode resilient CSS.
findings.evidence: The language control exposes 13 locales, but stylesheet inspection found zero logical-property rules and five physical left/right rules; html has lang=en but no explicit dir.
findings.suggestedFix: Set dir with locale, replace physical layout properties with logical equivalents, and test an RTL locale plus long translated labels.

findings.summary: Empty signup submission fails without visible or announced feedback.
findings.evidence: After rejecting consent and activating Sign up with all fields empty, the page remained unchanged: no :invalid fields, no alert/error nodes, and no focused invalid control.
findings.suggestedFix: Use native required constraints or post-interaction validation, show field-specific guidance, move focus to the first error, and announce a summary through a live region.

findings.summary: Decorative and sample media are substantially over-delivered.
findings.evidence: The image audit found 8 oversized images, 9 without responsive sources, 21 legacy-format assets and 7 eager below-fold images; HAR shows 4.47MB image transfer.
findings.suggestedFix: Generate responsive AVIF/WebP variants, use sizes/srcset, lazy-load below-fold media, and avoid multi-megabyte PNGs for small rendered elements.

findings.summary: Background media continues despite an explicit reduced-motion preference.
findings.evidence: The muted hero video autoplays without controls and continued advancing under reduced motion; this spends network and decode work before user intent.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a static poster by default under reduced motion/data-saving conditions and start media only when visible and useful.

findings.summary: Third-party and media cost is disproportionate to the landing task.
findings.evidence: HAR records 6.01MB cross-origin transfer, including multi-megabyte images, autoplay video requests, and 176KB Google Tag Manager before interaction.
findings.suggestedFix: Set an explicit route budget, defer nonessential third parties/media, and load marketing proof and ratings near viewport entry.

findings.summary: The background-removal capability is not exposed as a structured agent tool.
findings.evidence: The page has an upload form but no WebMCP registration, agentic form metadata, schema tool hints, or equivalent structured capability.
findings.suggestedFix: Offer a narrowly scoped agent tool that declares accepted image inputs, consent, cost, result format, and confirmation boundaries.
